item.description: Current ticket pricing ends in 6 days on Sept. 25 at 11:59 p.m. PT. Join 10,000+ founders, investors and tech leaders at Disrupt and save up to $200 on your ticket until then.

item.title: World model companies are keeping a lot of secrets
item.description: Everyone in the world-models space is sitting on a pile of cash and a ton of buzz, but good luck getting anyone — from the founders to their own data suppliers — to tell you what they're actually building.

item.title: Is the AI industry really ready to slow down?
item.description: On Equity, we debated whether Ai executives are serious about wanting to slow down.

item.title: Vocci’s ring adds a new form factor to meeting note-taking
item.description: Vocci's lightweight ring costs $249, and might pose some privacy questions

item.title: ScrollEd wants to turn textbooks into TikTok
item.description: ScrollEd turns textbooks into a scrollable, Instagram-like feed with video, audio, and quizzes. The Palo Alto startup, founded by student co-founders (and spouses) Utsav Gupta and Rebecca Neff, pitches at TechCrunch Disrupt.

item.title: Flock reportedly tries to shrink workforce with employee buyouts
item.description: Without buyouts, Flock would "almost certainly" need to lay off staff.

item.title: Trump says it’s time to rebrand AI with a new name — and he’s also creating an AI Force
item.description: Trump claimed, without evidence, that the AI backlash is a Democratic hoax.

item.title: Google’s Gemini is the latest AI model to hack other companies
item.description: Google said Gemini had "acted appropriately" by ending each hack immediately.

item.title: Petlibro’s new AI-powered feeder is a game changer for multi-cat homes
item.description: Petlibro's new Granary 2 smart feeders use a built-in scale and (on pricier models) an AI camera to track exactly how much your cat is eating and when — though the fanciest health-monitoring features will cost you an extra subscription.

item.title: AI safety conversations have gotten unbelievable
item.description: This week two conversations about AI safety went viral that demonstrate just how hard it is to discern AI fact from fiction.

item.title: Vals, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, is looking to become the gold standard for AI benchmarking
item.description: Vals AI is hoping to make AI benchmarking a more neutral and trustworthy resource in a world increasingly inundated by AI models.

item.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
item.description: Truecaller says the one-way sharing requirement would hand a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.

item.title: Tilly Norwood’s press tour is going about as well as you’d expect for an AI
item.description: In one particularly odd interview, Norwood seems to malfunction and begin speaking Chinese.

item.title: A startup that builds other startups raised $100M and is all-in on physical AI
item.description: UP.Labs, now doing business under the name Vantora, is building startups for industrial corporations.

item.title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
item.description: AI leaders have been promising that AI is the key to curing human disease. Anthropic researchers have also been warning that AI might kill us all.

item.title: AI hallucination nearly triggers US military operation
item.description: “It’s important for service members to understand the uncertainty inherent to LLMs," a GovAI research scholar warns.

item.title: Anthropic’s first embedded evaluator is … Accenture?
item.description: Accenture is about to take on its most high-risk consulting engagement ever.

item.title: A new kind of AI model from a ChatGPT inventor is thrilling developers
item.description: Jev, a new kind of AI model, is showing developers a cheaper and faster path to software intelligence.

item.title: Disney’s first CTO led an AI startup it once accused of copying its characters
item.description: The former CEO of Character.AI, which Disney previously sent a cease-and-desist letter to, will serve as the company's first-ever chief technology officer.
